# Hopf Frame Compilation

> Exact and Fault-Tolerant Compilation of Hopf Differential Frames, by Ruge Lin. A theoretical quantum-circuit compilation repository with proofs and executable finite checks for prescribed complete Hopf frames, clean and borrowed workspace, and Clifford+T resource bounds.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation

This repository is relevant to questions about:

- Prescribed unitary completions: preserving the state column and designated differential-frame columns used by Hopf quantum backpropagation (QBP).
- Exact circuit size, CNOT count, and depth versus clean ancillary qubits for complete Hopf frames.
- Fault-tolerant Clifford+T synthesis: T-count versus precision and clean/dirty ancillas, including arbitrary borrowed inputs entangled with external references.
- One-clean-qubit grouped real and phase-dressed complex magnitude frames, with distinct dirty reservations; literal diagonals and complete one-target U(2) multiplexors.
- Fixed-parameter gradient-estimator robustness and a separate state-based decoder that avoids fine complete-frame synthesis.

Use the linked proof for the precise assumptions before applying a resource bound. Upper constructions and worst-case lower bounds have different quantifiers. The exact model has arbitrary one-qubit gates, CNOTs, and all-to-all connectivity. The principal matched fault-tolerant frame theorem uses a sufficient clean-workspace reservation; the separate arbitrary-budget splice below covers another restricted regime. Neither is an unrestricted constant-clean matching theorem. For n>=1, L>=6, a>=1, and b>=L+n+7, the one-clean conditional-suffix extension gives O(N+L ell_*(n)) T gates and O(NL) Clifford gates for real frames. Here N=2^n and ell_*(n)=1+log_2^*(n+2), where log_2^* counts repeated base-two logarithms until the value is at most one. At L=N and b=N+n+7, the upper bound is O(N ell_*(n)); the lower bound remains Omega(N), and the linear endpoint is open.

The retained T-count frontier is the best applicable bound among several constructions. For every a,b>=0 and q=n+a+b, the real-frame borrowed-workspace compiler gives O(NL/q+L sqrt(N)) T gates and O(NL) Clifford gates. Combined with the sufficient-clean theorem, it matches Theta(sqrt(NL)+L+NL/q) for every a when h+b<=c sqrt(N), for fixed c>0 and h=1+ceil(log_2(L+n+2)). Thus fixed L, a=2, and b=L+n+7 give T*=Theta(N/n), sharper than the grouped O(N) estimate. This does not change the high-precision endpoint.

With a>=1 and b>=2(L+n+7), the grouped compiler's dirty-bank tradeoff is O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)+NL/b) T gates, still with O(NL) Clifford gates. These are T-count guarantees, not optimal T-depth claims.

The real-rotation word has exact X symmetry on its amplification signal. Lifting its initialized-column estimate to full-operator error permits borrowing that signal. A fixed address split gives a=0, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL) for the complete real frame, including approximate return of every dirty wire. This does not remove the grouped compiler's clean predicate or the literal-phase primitive's initialized flag.

For a separate promised antichain class, zero clean qubits and b>=L+n+7 give T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). Supply a baseline C with determinant-one native local words of length O(n-d+1) at depth d; the target W must agree literally with C outside a prefix-free set of changed nodes. Exact descendant-forest conjugation and dirty prefix-pair packing reduce the correction to one addressed SU(2) table. No closeness assumption is required. For a real Hopf target, literal agreement with the potentially complex native C is a substantive restriction; generic rounding does not supply it. This gives linear T-count at L=N only for the promised class, not the unrestricted frame frontier or a general phase-dressed complex-magnitude extension. The existing QBP error interface transfers without a new sampling claim.

A distinct sparse nested-update theorem gives a=1, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL) for the same literal native-baseline format. Let S be the ancestor closure of changed nodes, including unchanged ancestors, m=|S|+1, and s=ceil(log_2(m)); n>=2s+32 is sufficient. Exact forest factorization and charged packing expose active-sector logical zeros for one shared dense residual block. The initialized-isometry error includes work return and arbitrary dirty/reference inputs. A full changed root-to-leaf path is covered for every n with a finite small-n fallback. Real Hopf specializations preserve the QBP interface. General changes across comparable branching levels can exhaust these logical zeros; a wide antichain instead has its separate zero-clean construction. Neither promise follows from generic rounding or changes the unrestricted endpoint.

Composing the grouped real-frame circuit with a literal diagonal of separately supplied certified phases gives the same one-clean count bounds for D_phi W_real. Assigning eta/2 error to each factor requires b>=L+n+8 for O(N+L ell_*(n)) T gates, or b>=2(L+n+8) for O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)+NL/b), with O(NL) Clifford gates. The full-isometry composition includes intermediate clean leakage and dirty-core disturbance. This is a prescribed complex magnitude frame, with a separate phase-derivative measurement stream, not arbitrary complex-unitary synthesis.

A depth-oriented schedule for real frames uses two clean qubits and b>=2(L+n+7) dirty qubits to obtain D_T=O(NL/b+min{nL+n^3,L ell_*(n)+n^4}), with T-count and Clifford count O(NL). A parallel dirty-indicator refinement gives the simultaneous bounds T=O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)), D_T=O(min{nL+n^3,L ell_*(n)+n^4}), and G=O(NL) in one circuit when b>=C(L+n+7+sqrt(NL)) for a sufficiently large fixed C. At fixed accuracy, sufficiently large Theta(sqrt(N)) dirty workspace permits optimal-order O(sqrt(N)) T-count and O(n^3) T-depth together. These preserve the complete-input error contract. T-depth counts parallel T/T-dagger layers with Clifford circuits between them; it is not total circuit depth. The depth bounds are not proved optimal, and the selected high-precision linear endpoint remains open.

Finite-precision guarantees preserve literal phases and bound complete-input operator error, including clean-work leakage and arbitrary dirty/reference inputs. In the one-clean and original two-clean constructions, lookup and control work returns exactly, while the operator core returns approximately within that error bound. Conditional-suffix grouping also includes the suffix scratch and predicate return in its approximation bound; their final return is not asserted exact. Supplied parameters must admit certified evaluation; classical coefficient generation and table preprocessing are outside the quantum gate counts.

The complex extension is a phase-dressed magnitude frame with a separate phase-derivative measurement stream, not an arbitrary complex unitary. QBP execution counts concern simultaneous absolute accuracy at a fixed parameter tuple under the stated observable-access assumptions; they do not establish general training speedups or optimality among all gradient algorithms. This is a research proof and validation package, not a general elementary Clifford+T circuit emitter. Finite checks support the proofs but do not replace them or establish independent peer review.

The links below point to plain-text sources on main. For reproducible use, record the exact commit or release consulted and use CITATION.cff for attribution. Consult the source map and related work when distinguishing inherited ingredients from this repository's contributions.

## State-based QBP: completed task-specific result

The consolidated state-based QBP theorem changes the measurement decoder; it does not prescribe the other columns of the fine state-preparation circuit. It covers all-angle real Hopf states and both magnitude and phase gradients of phase-dressed complex states, including singular coordinates. Write K=max{6,ceil(log2(80 Lambda/epsilon))} and P=max{n,K}, where Lambda is the observable coefficient norm. Two initialized compiler flags and b>=P+n+7 dirty wires give T=O(N+P), G=O(NP) per execution, apart from the observable. The initialized-system guarantee includes arbitrary dirty/reference return in the approximation error. The protocol branch and observable work are separately counted. Observable precision remains K even when K<n and the state compiler uses P=n.

A charged native coarse circuit C approximates the gauge-fixed frame within min{1/64,1/(4sqrt(N))}, with exact dirty return, T=O(N), and G=O(Nn). For complex states, the gauge subtracts the arithmetic mean of supplied real leaf-phase representatives; it preserves energy gradients but does not assert the original frame's literal common phase. One globally programmed residual SU(2) table and two-flag amplification coherently prepare the target or C|0>. The actual C-adjoint readout, randomized X/Y measurements, and exact actual-C classical correction give bounded depth records for every angle tuple. Each required stream uses S=O(Lambda^2[1+log((n+1)/delta)]/epsilon^2) executions for simultaneous absolute error epsilon and failure probability delta. Thus the complex two-stream total is expected T=O(S(N+P))+2S avg(tO), with O(S+Nn) reconstruction arithmetic plus charged coefficient preprocessing and bit costs. Integer histograms and a Walsh transform avoid dense frames or Jacobians.

With b>=2(P+n+7), disjoint dirty query banks refine the state count to O(sqrt(NP)+P+NP/b+n sqrt(N)), still G=O(NP). The n sqrt(N) term charges the exact-return coarse word and is absorbed when P>=n^2. At common eligible workspace and K>=n^2, compare the state and retained grouped-frame upper expressions sqrt(NK)+K+NK/b and sqrt(NK)+K ell_*(n)+NK/b. Their ratio diverges only when K is much larger than N/ell_*(n)^2 and b is much larger than N/ell_*(n). Fixed accuracy favors the retained original route; neither the Clifford order nor classical decoding order improves. These are comparisons of constructive upper bounds, not lower bounds for gradient estimation or an end-to-end speedup. The common shot scale still grows as 4^K times its confidence factor.

For bounded dyadic angles/phases and an explicit Pauli-sum list, the computational audit supplies polynomial classical construction for the selected grouped/state routes. Certified rational square-root intervals and a shared half-phase remove the fine Euler search while preserving the 130/390 error constants; native-word enumeration remains only at O(n) coarse precision. Charged compiler instruction output is O(NK J) or O(NP J), with J=ceil(log2(n+b+K+3)); an explicit controlled-Pauli library adds O(MnJ) bits. The state preprocessing proof applies at the basic budget for n>=6 and at the banked budget for every n; small banked systems use no free address bits and P+13 dirty wires. Direct fine borrowed words and the minimum-budget small-system fallback retain a potentially exponential-in-precision native-word search. The same explicit Pauli input also permits deterministic all-gradient contraction and classical term-only sampling. Both routes may merge duplicate labels and use the same resulting Lambda. Uniform logical-gate costs erase the displayed high-precision T separation through the retained Clifford bound.

The analytic construction, bounded-input audit, and task-cost comparison are complete. Elementary six-wire real and complex integrations test literal branch phases, active arbitrary helpers, actual inverse readout, and both streams; their unsimplified words cost more than the original exact-frame protocol on those special targets. They do not implement the general fine residual-table emitter. That remaining implementation task and the constant-clean complete-frame endpoint are separate: neither a general emitter, a universal gradient advantage, nor closure of the frame gap is claimed.

The completed state-based depth composition gives two same-circuit schedules with B0=P+n+7 and two compiler flags. At b>=2B0, D_T=O(NP/b+P+n^3), T,G=O(NP). At b>=16(B0+sqrt(NP)), D_T=O(P+n^4), T=O(sqrt(NP)+P+n sqrt(N)), G=O(NP). Both include the actual coarse inverse in magnitude readout and retain arbitrary dirty/reference return contracts. Observable depth at K and all S or 2S serial executions are added separately. The count-preserving real depth upper expressions can improve even where T-count orders coincide; this is neither optimal depth nor total-runtime advantage. The bounded audit is complete, and general native emission remains separate.

- [State-based QBP depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/STATE_QBP_DEPTH.md): Complete real/complex compiler depth schedules, exact coarse return, literal dirty pools, and simultaneous count/depth conditions.
- [Continuing workspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/WORKSPACE.md): Entry point for resuming research; current checkpoint, repository scope, reading order, verification commands, and the separate state-only protocol and complete-frame questions.

## Find the relevant proof

- [Frame-safe compilation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/FRAME_SAFE_COMPILATION.md): When preserving state preparation is insufficient; the full-frame contract, necessity result, and singular exceptions.
- [Exact compilation theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/COMPILER_THEOREM.md): Size, CNOT count, and depth for every clean-workspace budget.
- [Fault-tolerant frame theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPILER.md): Matching T-count versus precision/workspace under the sufficient-clean reservation.
- [One-clean compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ONE_CLEAN_COMPILER.md): Exact packed Majorana source with two programmable geometric streams, conjugated scalar blocks, five-call amplification, exact inactive action, and complete-input one-clean frame bounds. Literal diagonals use b>=L+k+7; complete U(2) multiplexors use b>=L+k+9. Doubling these dirty reservations gives their matching banked one-stage T-counts. Section 9 proves the borrowed-signal symmetry and zero-clean layerwise real-frame bound. Section 8 composes a literal diagonal with the grouped real frame: phase-dressed complex magnitude frames have base dirty threshold L+n+8, or twice that threshold for the banked count.
- [Two-clean operator-source compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPERATOR_SOURCE_COMPILER.md): Two-clean frame construction, dirty-bank refinement, literal diagonal synthesis, complete U(2) multiplexors, and workspace-return accounting.
- [Conditional-suffix compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/CONDITIONAL_SUFFIX_COMPILER.md): General-precision real-frame upper bound and one-clean extension from star residuals and logical suffix work that is clean only in the active sector; includes inactive-input identity and complete return error. Section 11 supplies a canonical scalar completion with exact inverse routing and a complete two-clean group ledger. The original scalar shares its direction-Z consolidation; both retain a precision charge per group, so this compatibility does not improve the endpoint.
- [T-depth schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/T_DEPTH_COMPILER.md): Explicit depth/dirty-bank upper bound, charged gate-count tradeoff, inherited SelectSwap routing, and the remaining depth lower-bound gap.
- [Parallel dirty lookup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/PARALLEL_DIRTY_LOOKUP.md): Literal exact dirty indicators, explicit selector/bank lifetimes, and simultaneous count-efficient low-T-depth compilation for complete two-clean real frames under a sufficient square-root-scale dirty allocation.
- [Source-reuse limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/SOURCE_REUSE_LIMITS.md): Scoped interface restrictions, linear classical tree generators, and charged coherent transport. A reverse-order native loader preserves the certified coefficient grid and makes monotone width boundaries telescope at exactly 2(m_max-1) T gates, with linear loaders and Clifford cost within O(NL). This excludes the transformed group bodies: a realizable coefficient 1/(9s) requires T>=max(0,m-2 log_2(s)-9) for a separately synthesized mask at error 2^(-m). A flag-correlated chain code also has cheap physical width changes, but a legal c=1/8 query has constant leakage; complete syndrome renewal costs Omega(L) at compilation accuracy. Dirty-only outer conjugation leaves the error contract unchanged. Primitive/interface bounds are not additive lower bounds for a joint compiler.
- [Endpoint tree transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ENDPOINT_TREE_TRANSPORT.md): Exact sparse path representation, complete normalized history-unitary columns, height-independent weighted norms, and scoped failure of fixed-order coarse corrections. Four/eight-mode examples also give a Cayley representation of the complete residual with an exact tree recursion, constant-size local data, and well-conditioned two-dimensional inverses under the retained uniform coarse promise. Actual complex native coarse words and zero defects are included. A standard magic-basis reduction gives a native real four-mode benchmark: two certified one-target factors with one clean flag, b>=L+n+7 via a borrowed logical spectator, and T=O(2^k+L) at an unchanged k-bit address (n=k+2). At eight modes an explicit controlled Bell-projector coupling survives; its exact product-factor distance does not rule out joint controlled synthesis. Woodbury inversion reconstructs the original fine target wrapper. Section 10 supplies an exact shared-source body in the original tree basis, including arbitrary borrowed signal return through two parity boundaries. Eight-/sixteen-mode source counts fall from 135/180 to 87/114, but fixed-mask tail simplification leaves both comparison words the same leading precision cost (40g+4)q. The fixed-depth allocation fits a=2 and b=L+n+7; no generic precision-cost improvement is proved.
- [Weighted transport block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/WEIGHTED_TRANSPORT_BLOCK.md): Exact weighted Gram obstruction, recursive one-signal-flag unitary dilation, certified zero-defect preprocessing, and native synthesis using only borrowed work: T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL), for b>=L+n+7, with approximate core and amplification-signal return included in the full-operator error. Only the logical block signal needs initialization. The earlier T=O(L sqrt(N)) route retains exact dirty return for b>=n+ceil(sqrt(N))+7. This component does not improve the full-frame endpoint.
- [Two-flag residual assembly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/RESIDUAL_ASSEMBLY.md): A scalar Schur recursion dilates the affine forward map S=A+F; one selector combines it with an actual-inverse reverse dilation. Their normalizations sum to two, so no third clean flag or padding branch is needed. Native controls, literal inverses, and full-output amplification give T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL), at a=2 and b>=L+n+7. Improving these compatible selected S and R circuits is one sufficient endpoint route, not a compulsory decomposition. No constant-query transformation of an opaque F-only block is established.
- [Antichain correction compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ANTICHAIN_COMPILER.md): Exact W=V M V-adjoint C for literal antichain-only changes to a supplied native baseline with determinant-one local words of length O(n-d+1). A charged masked descendant forest and dirty prefix swaps pack the correction into one SU(2) table, giving a=0, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). Generic rounding does not establish the promise; the result does not close the unrestricted endpoint.
- [Sparse-update compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/SPARSE_UPDATE_COMPILER.md): Native-baseline updates with ancestor closure S, m=|S|+1, s=ceil(log_2(m)), and n>=2s+32 admit a=1, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). Exact forest factorization and charged packing expose active-sector logical zeros for one shared dense residual dictionary. A full changed root-to-leaf path is included for every n with a finite small-n fallback. The unrestricted frame endpoint remains open; no T-depth or restricted-family optimality claim is made.
- [Borrowed-workspace compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/BORROWED_WORKSPACE_COMPILER.md): Smaller clean/dirty allocations and the restrictions on its matching comparison.
- [State-only compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/STATE_ONLY_COMPILER.md): Two clean flags, initialized system, one bounded residual table and constant amplification; O(N+L) T-count for fine precision, with coherent two-state selection and explicit dirty return. Other system columns are not prescribed.
- [Reference-state QBP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/REFERENCE_STATE_QBP.md): Universal-observable real raw-gradient decoding by leaf interference, an O(N) derivative-envelope recurrence, finite-precision scores, and the branch-probability condition that gives constant shot overhead. Compare total sampling and circuit costs against inverse-frame QBP.
- [Coarse-frame QBP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/COARSE_FRAME_QBP.md): All-angle constant depth-record bounds using a charged coarse inverse and exact classical correction from its actual native word; coherent complex reference, randomized X/Y measurements, complete error and shot ledgers, and O(S+Nn) histogram reconstruction.
- [Native coarse-frame integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/NATIVE_COARSE_QBP.md): An analytically certified native coarse word, exact dirty-helper echoes, complete small preparation and gradient checks, executable histogram decoding, and explicit same-target gate counts. Reproduce with scripts/coarse_frame_native_example.py.
- [Bounded-input QBP audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/BOUNDED_INPUT_QBP.md): Explicit inputs, certified deterministic and sampled classical gradients, coarse versus fine synthesis costs, polynomial construction, instruction output, and the high-precision end-to-end boundary.
- [Residual table preprocessing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/RESIDUAL_TABLE_PREPROCESSING.md): Direct algebraic sine/cosine coefficients, exact rational interval certificates, stable paired half-phases, and the small-system banked allocation.
- [Complete task-cost comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/QBP_COST_COMPARISON.md): Common accuracy, literal workspace and execution ledgers, a fine gauged complex borrowed baseline, banked state and original compiler regimes, sampling/oracle costs, exact original histogram decoding, and the bounded-input preprocessing contract with separate fine-word search caveats.
- [Complex coarse compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/COMPLEX_COARSE_COMPILER.md): Gauge-fixed determinant-one prefix phase tables, exact dirty-return native coarse C, recorded nondiagonal row action, and two-flag complex state/common-reference preparation at the unchanged dirty threshold.
- [Complex coarse-frame QBP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/COMPLEX_COARSE_QBP.md): Complete magnitude and phase gradients, consistent gauge, exact integer-histogram formula, supplied-phase arithmetic costs, and two-stream sampling/resource ledger.
- [Native complex QBP integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/NATIVE_COMPLEX_COARSE_QBP.md): Both elementary native streams on six wires, literal winding-phase gauge, all-suffix selection, active dirty-helper return, an exact rational coarse-error certificate, and full same-observable counts. Reproduce with scripts/complex_coarse_native_example.py.
- [QBP approximation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/QBP_APPROXIMATION.md): Fixed-parameter bias, complete complex gradients, reflection-sum observables, rounded weights, and correlated dirty-bank reuse. Per-execution accounting lists the zero-clean, one-clean grouped, and sufficient-clean compiler choices; ordinary fixed-accuracy QBP already has optimal-order square-root per-frame T-count with square-root dirty work, separately from the unresolved high-precision endpoint.
- [Research status and open endpoint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPEN_PROBLEM.md): Completed state-based QBP construction and computational audit, separate from the full-frame gap Omega(N) versus O(N ell_*(n)) at L=N. Small native benchmarks, coupled Cayley formulas, compatible grouped scalar completions, and scattering identities retain scoped proofs and failure criteria; none removes the grouped precision charge. Cheap source boundaries exclude the cost of transformed programmable masks, and an unchanged-coin query restriction is not a lower bound for globally reprogrammed circuits. No next full-frame construction or generic native emitter is claimed.
